content.text:
The campaign is done and I submitted **index 2** (Bi 0.22, Cu 0.30, V 0.48). At 4.47×10⁻⁵ A it had the highest photocurrent of the three compositions I measured. I used all 3 merit measurements and all 5 XRD measurements.

| Index | Composition (Bi / Cu / V) | Phases from XRD | Photocurrent |
|---|---|---|---|
| 7 | 0.40 / 0.19 / 0.41 | mostly BiVO₄ | 1.24×10⁻⁶ A |
| **2** | 0.22 / 0.30 / 0.48 | BiVO₄ plus a second phase (peak at Q≈1.746) | **4.47×10⁻⁵ A** |
| 4 | 0.18 / 0.34 / 0.48 | same as index 2 | 3.73×10⁻⁵ A |

- **Starting point:** I began with the high-bismuth region because bismuth vanadate (BiVO₄) is the standard photoanode in this system. Index 7 was almost pure BiVO₄ but performed poorly.
- **What worked better:** Adding copper and vanadium brought in a second phase, probably a copper vanadate. That film (index 2) gave about 36 times more current than index 7.
- **Where the best spot likely sits:** Index 4 has the same two phases with less bismuth, and its current dropped. So the best point is probably at or near index 2.
- **What I ruled out without measuring:**
  - Index 41 loses the second phase that the best films share and picks up other phases.
  - Index 46, in the copper-rich corner, has no BiVO₄ at all.

The main gap: with only 3 merit measurements, I didn't measure index 6, which sits between indices 2 and 4. The true best composition in the library could be slightly different from index 2.
